title: Buying Your First UK Home? Five Benefits Indian Professionals Should Know
excerpt: From stamp duty relief to Lifetime ISAs, a guide to the schemes that can save Indian-origin first-time buyers tens of thousands of pounds in 2026
body:
The United Kingdom remains one of the top destinations for Indian professionals, with an estimated 900,000 Indian-born residents now calling Britain home. For many, the leap from renting to owning is the defining financial milestone — and in 2026, the UK government offers several programs designed to make that jump more achievable.

**Stamp Duty Relief:** First-time buyers in England and Northern Ireland pay zero Stamp Duty Land Tax on properties up to 300,000 pounds, effective from April 2026. For homes priced between 300,001 and 500,000 pounds, a reduced rate of 5% applies only to the portion above the threshold. On a 400,000-pound home — roughly average for London's outer boroughs where many Indian professionals settle — this saves 5,000 pounds compared to standard rates. Scotland offers separate relief through its Land and Buildings Transaction Tax, with a nil-rate threshold of 175,000 pounds.

**The Lifetime ISA:** Indian-origin buyers under 40 can open a Lifetime ISA and deposit up to 4,000 pounds annually toward a first home. The government adds a 25% bonus — effectively 1,000 pounds of free money per year. Over five years of maximum contributions, that is 5,000 pounds in bonuses alone. The account can be used for properties up to 450,000 pounds, making it viable for most purchases outside central London.

**Shared Ownership:** For those priced out of full ownership, Shared Ownership lets buyers purchase a 10% to 75% share of a home and pay rent on the remainder. This dramatically reduces the deposit needed — a 5% deposit on a 25% share of a 300,000-pound home is just 3,750 pounds. Many housing associations in areas with large Indian communities, including Leicester, Birmingham, and parts of West London, actively market shared ownership properties.

**Mortgage Guarantee Scheme:** The government-backed scheme allows lenders to offer 95% loan-to-value mortgages, meaning buyers need only a 5% deposit. For Indian professionals on skilled worker visas or those who recently obtained indefinite leave to remain, this lowers the barrier to entry significantly — though visa status can affect mortgage eligibility, and specialist brokers familiar with immigration pathways are worth consulting.

**First Homes Discount:** The First Homes scheme offers new-build properties at a minimum 30% discount to market value, with some local authorities offering up to 50%. Priority goes to key workers and local residents. Indian-origin NHS staff, teachers, and public sector employees are particularly well-positioned to benefit, especially in areas outside London where discounted prices can bring homes below 200,000 pounds.

**What to Watch:** The stamp duty relief thresholds have fluctuated repeatedly since 2017 — buyers should act while current rates hold, as any autumn budget could reset them.
nri_angle: With 900,000 Indian-born UK residents, first-time buyer schemes are directly relevant to professionals on skilled worker visas and those who recently settled.
author: Diaspora Desk
